nodes.name: On unhandled failure
nodes.notes: Fires only for failures the main workflow did NOT handle itself. Expected failures (a typed error from /qualify, exhausted transport retries) are dead-lettered on the main workflow's own error branch with full context, which also lets the caller get a real HTTP response. This is the net underneath that: Postgres down, an expression blowing up, and so on.

nodes.name: Extract Failure Context
nodes.notes: Records what the Error Trigger actually exposes rather than inventing a domain.

nodes.name: Write Dead Letter

parameters.query:
-- Safety net only. The main workflow handles every *expected* failure on its
-- own error branch with full context; this fires for unhandled node failures
-- (e.g. Postgres itself unreachable), where the Error Trigger exposes the
-- execution context but not the original webhook payload.
INSERT INTO dead_letters
  (domain, idempotency_key, failure_stage, last_error, attempt_count, payload_snapshot)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6::jsonb)
RETURNING id, failure_stage, created_at;

nodes.notes:
SELECT * FROM dead_letters WHERE failure_stage = 'unknown' shows these.

Select the 'Lead Qualifier Postgres' credential on this node after import.
